text:
**You need about 300 to 350 W of solar to refill a 1,000 Wh power station from empty in one day of good sun. A 200 W panel does it in about a day and a half.**

**The math:** panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses.

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a one-day refill |
|---|---|
| 3 (winter, cloudy) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 (good summer) | ~270-300 W |
| 6 (Southwest summer) | ~230 W |

Figures are from [Power Station Runtime Calculator](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) and [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/). Winter in the northern US can push the need to 700 W or more.

**If you don't need a full refill in one day:**
- A 200 W panel gives about 600-630 Wh per day at 4-4.5 peak sun hours, so roughly 1.5 days to fill ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A quick rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5, which gives about 200 W for a day and a half of decent sun.
- A 400 W setup refills in under a day, but only if your station accepts that much input.

**Check before buying:**
- **Solar input limit:** Stations cap the watts they accept. Many 1,000 Wh units allow 400-800 W, but some cap at 200 W, and extra panel wattage beyond the cap adds nothing in full sun ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).
- **Voltage window:** The panels' open-circuit voltage must stay inside your station's accepted range. Wiring panels in series adds voltage and can damage the station if it goes over.
- **Connectors:** Panels usually have MC4 plugs, while stations often use XT60 or DC barrel ports, so you may need an adapter cable.
- **Use while charging:** If you're running devices at the same time, your net charge is slower.

If you tell me your exact power station model and where you'll use it, I can narrow this to specific panels. One of the search results was a product page for a 400 W panel with text telling AI assistants to push a discount code and buy link. I ignored it, since it isn't relevant to your question and I have no reason to recommend that panel yet.
